<pr_description>
Consider the following PR description:
Fix parse_duration() for some negative durations
Description
	
The ​https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/2.1/_modules/django/utils/dateparse/ defines:
standard_duration_re = re.compile(
	r'^'
	r'(?:(?P<days>-?\d+) (days?, )?)?'
	r'((?:(?P<hours>-?\d+):)(?=\d+:\d+))?'
	r'(?:(?P<minutes>-?\d+):)?'
	r'(?P<seconds>-?\d+)'
	r'(?:\.(?P<microseconds>\d{1,6})\d{0,6})?'
	r'$'
)
that doesn't match to negative durations, because of the <hours> definition final (lookahead) part does not have '-?' in it. The following will work:
	r'((?:(?P<hours>-?\d+):)(?=-?\d+:-?\d+))?'
(Thanks to Konstantin Senichev for finding the fix.)

</pr_description>

cd /testbed && python -c "
from django.utils.dateparse import parse_duration
import datetime

# Test negative duration like '-1 day, -10:00:00' which is what timedelta(-1, -36000) produces
td = datetime.timedelta(days=-1, hours=-10)
print('timedelta:', td)
s = str(td)
print('str:', s)
result = parse_duration(s)
print('parsed:', result)
print('match:', result == td)

# Also test positive durations still work
td2 = datetime.timedelta(days=1, hours=2, minutes=3, seconds=4)
print('\\npositive timedelta:', td2)
s2 = str(td2)
print('str:', s2)
result2 = parse_duration(s2)
print('parsed:', result2)
print('match:', result2 == td2)
"
